title: 8 Best AI Database Tools for Solopreneurs in 2026: Airtable Alternatives Compared
description: Compare the 8 best AI database tools for solopreneurs in 2026 — Airtable, Notion DB, Coda, Baserow, NocoDB, Supabase, Rowy, and DronaHQ. Find the best Airtable alternative for your solo business with real pricing and feature comparisons.
content:
## Introduction

If you're running a solo business in 2026, your database is the engine room of the whole operation. Customer lists, inventory tracking, content calendars, project pipelines, affiliate records — it all lives somewhere, and the wrong tool turns a simple lookup into a headache. Airtable has long been the default for solopreneurs who want spreadsheet simplicity with database power, but the landscape has changed. With AI features baked into nearly every tier, open-source options that rival proprietary platforms, and pricing ranging from free to hundreds a month, choosing the right tool requires real numbers.

I tested eight AI database tools — Airtable, Notion Databases, Coda, Baserow, NocoDB, Supabase, Rowy, and DronaHQ — to find which ones actually deliver for a one-person operation. Prices are current as of June 2026.

---

## Tool Deep Dives

### 1. Airtable

Airtable is still the heavyweight in no-code databases. Its grid, calendar, kanban, and gallery views are polished, and the 2026 releases added native AI autofill that generates descriptions, categorizes records, and drafts copy based on patterns in your data.

**Pricing:** Free tier gives 1,000 records per base and 2 GB of attachments. Team plan is $24/seat/month (annual) and removes most record limits. Business plan at $54/seat unlocks advanced sync, custom branded forms, and the AI copilot.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs who need a polished tool with zero learning curve. If you share filtered views with clients, Airtable's interface is hard to beat.

**The catch:** Per-seat pricing stings when you're a team of one.

---

### 2. Notion Databases

Notion evolved its database functionality significantly. You get rollups, formulas, linked databases, and a query engine supporting filtered aggregations across hundreds of thousands of rows. The 2026 AI features include smart property suggestions and a natural-language query bar.

**Pricing:** Free for individuals with unlimited pages. Plus plan is $12/month (annual). AI add-on is $10/month per workspace.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs already living inside Notion. If your CRM, content calendar, and project tracker are all in Notion, adding databases avoids context-switching.

**The catch:** Performance degrades past about 10,000 rows, and it's not a true relational database.

---

### 3. Coda

Coda combines documents, spreadsheets, and databases into one canvas. Its "Packs" ecosystem is deeper than any competitor — you can pull Stripe data or send Slack messages directly inside a doc. The 2026 AI assistant generates tables from text prompts and builds formulas by description.

**Pricing:** Free tier allows 50 objects and 1,000 rows per doc. Pro plan at $12/month bumps to unlimited docs and 50,000 rows per doc. Team plan at $30/month adds automations.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs who need a hybrid workspace — part documentation, part database, part automation hub.

**The catch:** Real learning curve, and it's the slowest of the eight on large documents.

---

### 4. Baserow

Baserow is an open-source Airtable alternative you can self-host or use via their cloud. It offers grid, kanban, gallery, and form views with a clean, fast interface. The 2026 releases include an API-first mode and conditional formatting.

**Pricing:** Self-hosted is completely free and unlimited. Cloud free tier caps at 2,000 rows per workspace. Premium plan at $10/user/month gives 50,000 rows.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs who want control and don't mind self-hosting. Spin up a Docker container on a $5 VPS for unlimited rows.

**The catch:** Self-hosting means you handle backups and updates. No mobile app, and forms are basic.

---

### 5. NocoDB

NocoDB turns any MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or SQLite database into a smart spreadsheet with an auto-generated REST API. The 2026 version introduced AI-assisted formula generation and a new dashboard builder.

**Pricing:** Self-hosted is free (MIT license). Cloud starts at $10/month for 5,000 records, up to $50/month for 100,000. Free tier includes 1,000 records.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs with existing databases who want a spreadsheet frontend without vendor lock-in.

**The catch:** The UI is functional but not beautiful. Non-technical users may struggle with setup.

---

### 6. Supabase

Supabase is an open-source Firebase alternative: PostgreSQL database with built-in REST API, real-time subscriptions, auth, storage, and edge functions. The 2026 AI Assistant generates schemas from natural-language descriptions.

**Pricing:** Free tier includes 500 MB database, 2 GB storage. Pro plan at $25/month bumps to 8 GB database and 100 GB bandwidth.

**Best for:** Technical solopreneurs building a product. Supabase is the most complete option if you're shipping a SaaS or marketplace.

**The catch:** Real database complexity. No spreadsheet-style grid for non-technical users.

---

### 7. Rowy

Rowy provides a spreadsheet UI on top of Firestore or PostgreSQL, with built-in automations and cloud functions. You can write JavaScript column formulas and deploy serverless functions from the spreadsheet.

**Pricing:** Free tier includes 1,000 rows. Growth plan at $29/month unlocks 50,000 rows and custom roles.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs building on Firebase who want a visual database manager.

**The catch:** Still maturing — UI can be buggy on large datasets. Best for Firebase-native projects.

---

### 8. DronaHQ

DronaHQ is a low-code internal tool platform with a powerful database module. You get a visual database builder with forms, tables, and workflows, plus 200+ integrations. The 2026 version added AI-powered form generation.

**Pricing:** Free tier includes 2 users and 100 MB data. Business plan at $30/user/month (annual) unlocks unlimited apps and 1 GB data.

**Best for:** Solopreneurs building multiple internal tools — dashboards, approval systems, client portals — without code.

**The catch:** Per-user pricing hurts solopreneurs, and the learning curve is steep.

## FAQ

### 1. Which tool is best for a non-technical solopreneur?

Airtable or Notion Databases. Both have the shallowest learning curves, the best mobile apps, and the most intuitive interfaces. If you already use Notion for notes and project management, stick with Notion DB — the integration is seamless. If you prefer a dedicated database tool with professional views you can share with clients, go with Airtable.

### 2. Can I switch from Airtable to an open-source tool without losing data?

Yes, but ease depends on complexity. NocoDB and Baserow both offer Airtable import tools, though linked records and attachments have varying success. For simple tables under 5,000 rows, migration is smooth. For complex bases with linked records and automations, expect a weekend of manual cleanup.

### 3. Do I really need AI features, or is it just hype?

The AI features that matter save you typing. Airtable's AI autofill reduces data entry time categorizing products or writing descriptions. Coda and Notion's query bars help when you can't remember where you filed something. Schema generators in Supabase and NocoDB are niche — great for building from scratch, irrelevant if your data structure is set. Don't pay extra for AI you won't use daily.

### 4. What's the cheapest way to get unlimited rows?

Self-host Baserow on a $5–$10/month VPS for unlimited rows and full data control. NocoDB is a close second if you already run a MySQL or PostgreSQL database. If you don't want server management, Supabase's $25/month Pro plan gives 8 GB of database storage — enough for hundreds of thousands of rows — plus auth, storage, and real-time features.

### 5. Which tool is best for a solo founder building a SaaS?

Supabase, no contest. Production-grade PostgreSQL, authentication, real-time subscriptions, storage, and edge functions in one platform. The free tier handles an MVP, and Pro scales cleanly to paying customers. Rowy is worth a look for Firebase-native projects, but Supabase's PostgreSQL foundation gives a clearer path to a multi-developer team later.

---

## Summary

There is no single best AI database tool for every solopreneur. Here's the short version:

- **Non-technical, want polish:** Airtable or Notion DB.
- **Budget-conscious, can self-host:** Baserow or NocoDB.
- **Solo founder building a product:** Supabase.
- **Firebase-native projects:** Rowy.
- **Hybrid docs and databases:** Coda.
- **Multiple internal tools:** DronaHQ.

The trend in 2026 is clear: open-source tools like Baserow, NocoDB, and Supabase have closed the feature gap with proprietary platforms while offering better pricing and data ownership. If you're starting a project today, go with one of those three unless you have a specific reason to choose Airtable or Notion. Your future self — tired of per-seat pricing — will thank you.
